notes: The template voice layer: every sentence the city says. The sim decides what happens and passes facts; the voice only words them, so a different voice (another language, or a small local language model later) can replace this file without changing the game. Each key has one or more variants; one is picked from a hash of the event, so the choice never touches the simulation's random numbers. Placeholders in braces are filled from the facts; unknown ones are left as they are.

health.label: Kids who didn't cry at the jab

disaster.fire.start: Fire on {street}! Smoke is pouring out of a building and the sirens are on their way.
A fire has broken out on {street}. Neighbours are out on the pavement with garden hoses.
disaster.fire.end: The fire on {street} is out. {count} buildings were lost and {damaged} were singed.
Firefighters have put out the blaze near {street}: {count} buildings gone, {damaged} damaged.
disaster.tornado.start: Tornado! A funnel cloud has touched down near {street}. Hold on to your hats, and your roofs.
The sky over {street} has gone green. A tornado is on the ground.
disaster.tornado.end: The tornado has blown itself out. It destroyed {count} buildings and damaged {damaged}; check the power lines it tore down.
Calm again. The twister took {count} buildings and knocked {damaged} about, and it ripped up power lines on its way.
disaster.earthquake.start: Earthquake! The ground shook hard around {street}. Teacups everywhere are in pieces.
A quake centred under {street} rattled the whole city.
disaster.earthquake.end: The aftershocks have stopped. The quake brought down {count} buildings and cracked {damaged}.
Engineers have finished their survey: {count} buildings lost to the quake, {damaged} damaged.
disaster.robot.start: The Clockwork Colossus has wound itself up and is clanking towards {street}! Nobody knows who wound it.
A giant tin robot, key still turning in its back, has stomped into town heading for {street}.
disaster.robot.end: The Clockwork Colossus has run down at last and keeled over with a sad little 'ping'. It flattened {count} buildings and dented {damaged}.
The tin giant's spring is spent. It sits by {street} like a very large toy someone forgot. Toll: {count} buildings flattened, {damaged} dented.
petition-park: {name} and {count} neighbours on {street} have signed a petition: "Our kids are playing in the gutter. We'd like a park within walking distance."
A petition from {street}: {count} residents, led by {name}, ask for a park nearby. They've drawn a picture of it. It has a dragon.
petition-park.fulfilled: {street} has its park, and {name} cut the ribbon. The neighbours passed round a hat: ${amount} for the city.
petition-park.ignored: {name}'s park petition has expired unanswered. {street} grumbles.
petition-police: {name} of {street}: "Someone stole my garden gnome. Then my other garden gnome. We need police round here."
{count} residents on {street} want a police station closer to home after a run of bicycle thefts.
petition-police.fulfilled: Police now patrol {street}. {name}'s gnomes are safe at last.
petition-police.ignored: No police came to {street}. {name} has started guarding the gnomes personally.
petition-school: Parents on {street}, led by {name}, ask for a school their children can walk to.
{name} writes: "My kids take two buses to school. {count} of us on {street} want one nearby."
petition-school.fulfilled: Children on {street} can walk to school now. {name} has been elected head of the parents' committee, against their will.
petition-school.ignored: The school petition from {street} lapsed. Parents are not pleased.
petition-clinic: {name} on {street} sprained an ankle and limped three kilometres to the nearest doctor. {count} neighbours want a clinic closer.
petition-clinic.fulfilled: {street} has health care within reach. {name}'s ankle is much better, thank you.
petition-clinic.ignored: Still no clinic near {street}. {name} has bought a very large first aid kit.
petition-taxes: The {street} Residents' Association, chaired by {name}, demands residential taxes back down to 9%.
{count} households, led by {name} of {street}, say taxes are too high and want them cut to 9% or less.
petition-taxes.fulfilled: Taxes are down and {name} is throwing a street party on {street}.
petition-taxes.ignored: {name}'s tax petition was ignored. Letters to the editor have tripled.
petition-traffic: {name} spent forty minutes stuck on {street} this morning. {count} commuters have signed a petition to fix the traffic there.
Drivers on {street} want the jams sorted. {name} has brought a thermos and a sleeping bag to make the point.
petition-traffic.fulfilled: Traffic flows on {street} again. {name} got home in time for dinner.
petition-traffic.ignored: {street} is still jammed and {name}'s petition has lapsed.
petition-recycling: {name} and {count} others want a recycling program: "We're sorting our bottles by colour and nobody is collecting them."
petition-recycling.fulfilled: Recycling bins are out. {name} sorted three bags on the first day.
petition-recycling.ignored: No recycling program. {name}'s garage is now full of sorted bottles.
deal-casino: The Lucky Lug Nut Corporation wants to open a casino in {city}. They'll pay ${amount} up front and about $900 a month in fees. Your neighbours may not love the noise.
deal-casino.accepted: {city} said yes to the Lucky Lug Nut Casino. Find it under Place building.
deal-casino.declined: {city} turned down the casino. Somewhere, a slot machine weeps.
deal-toxic-dump: A regional waste firm offers ${amount} now and $1,500 a month to store "slightly glowing" waste in {city}. It will pollute the land and water around it.
deal-toxic-dump.accepted: The council voted to take the waste. The Toxic Waste Dump is under Place building. Please don't put it near anyone.
deal-toxic-dump.declined: {city} said no to the waste dump. Residents cheer, and wash their hands anyway.
deal-pickle-plant: Mega Pickle Inc. wants to build its biggest plant in {city}: 180 jobs, a whiff of vinegar, and a year of extra industrial demand while the suppliers move in.
deal-pickle-plant.accepted: Mega Pickle is coming to {city}. Find the plant under Place building.
deal-pickle-plant.declined: Mega Pickle will build elsewhere. The town smells unchanged.
deal-billboards: An advertising firm will pay $300 a month for a year to put billboards along {city}'s roads. Homes won't like the view.
deal-billboards.accepted: Billboards are going up. The first one sells toothpaste, aggressively.
deal-billboards.declined: No billboards for {city}. The skyline stays boring.
deal-sports-team: The {city} Thunderducks minor-league team asks for $400 a month for a year. In return: visitors, busy shops and a mascot.
deal-sports-team.accepted: The Thunderducks are staying. The mascot did a backflip and pulled a muscle.
deal-sports-team.declined: The Thunderducks will look for another town.
news-pie: {name} of {city} wins the regional pie contest with a rhubarb-and-mystery entry.
Pie-eating contest ends in a tie; judges eat the remaining pies to settle it.
news-weather: Weather: mild, with a chance of pigeons.
Weather: sunny spells and an unexplained smell of toast.
Forecast: rain, then more rain, then a rainbow the council will take credit for.
news-cat: A cat named Mayor Whiskers has been elected to the {city} library board (honorary, but she takes it seriously).
news-pothole: A pothole on {street} has been named Gerald by local children. Gerald is growing.
news-smog: Residents on {street} report the air tastes "a bit metallic". Pollution there is among the worst in {city}.
news-jobs: Job hunt: more than one in ten workers in {city} can't find work. Industry and shops could use more room to grow.
news.milestone: {city} reaches {population} people! The welcome sign has been repainted, slightly wonky.
news.ordinance.offered: Opportunity: {ordinance}. Decide in the Laws tab within {months} months.
news.abandoned: Boarded-up windows on {street}: a building there has been abandoned.
advisor.finance.red: We're ${amount} in the red. Raise a tax a little, trim funding on something nobody uses, or borrow.
advisor.finance.losing: We lost ${amount} last month. At this rate the treasury empties in about {months} months.
advisor.finance.taxes-high: Residential taxes average {percent}%. That's what people complain about at the bakery.
advisor.finance.ok: The books balance: we made ${amount} last month. I'm almost smiling.
advisor.utilities.no-power: We have zoned land and no power plant. Nothing will grow until we build one.
advisor.utilities.brownout: The grid is overloaded: {used} kW wanted, {capacity} kW made. Build a plant before the lights go out for good.
advisor.utilities.power-tight: Power is at {percent}% of capacity. Demand is being held back; a new plant would let the city grow.
advisor.utilities.water: The pumps can't keep up: {used} wanted, {capacity} pumped. Add a pump, away from industry.
advisor.utilities.garbage: Garbage is piling up: {amount} units a day nobody collects. A landfill with a road would fix it.
advisor.utilities.ok: Power at {percent}%, water flowing, bins emptied. Lovely.
advisor.planning.no-room: People want more {zone}, but there's nowhere to put it. Zone some near a road.
advisor.planning.stranded: {count} zoned cells are too far from a road to use. Add a road or rezone them.
advisor.planning.connect: We've no road to the region. A road off the edge of the map would bring shoppers, freight and new residents.
advisor.planning.ok: Demand is strongest for {zone}. Keep land ready for it.
advisor.safety.police: Only {percent}% of homes have police nearby. A station would cheer people up.
advisor.safety.health: Only {percent}% of homes are near health care. A clinic is cheap.
advisor.safety.schools: Only {percent}% of homes are near a school. Educated people want better jobs and bigger homes.
advisor.safety.approval: Approval is down to {percent}%. Answer a petition or two.
advisor.safety.ok: Homes are covered and people are mostly content. Approval: {percent}%.
advisor.transport.jam: {street} is jammed at {percent}% of capacity. A parallel road or a bigger one would help.
advisor.transport.pollution: Homes average {percent} pollution. The Clean Air Act or moving industry away would help.
advisor.transport.ok: Roads are flowing and the air is clean enough. Busiest road: {percent}% of capacity.
